convention_record_2026_09_29: Distances, balls and volumes are intrinsic to the carrier. The distance is over C1 paths in W; boundary covariant derivatives use fderivWithin (range I).
NearlyCuspidalBoundary.diameter is measured in the intrinsic distance of all W, not in the induced boundary metric; HyperbolicCusp.torusMetric is an arbitrary flat metric.
curvatureRadius is the extended Perelman rho from §7.3 lines 1091–1093. At top the finite-radius collapse predicate is vacuous; the new proved lemma records that fact.
The scale-volume condition follows Perelman (7.6), lines 1095–1099, and is stronger than the some-radius condition in KL92.3(1).
Whole-ball uncapped derivative tests are stronger than the center/radius-capped tests in KL92.3(3). WBD/TCF translations remain separate proof obligations; finite K is supported by Remark92.4.
The Lean derivative radius is strict r<rho, as PBR03 B:10287; the Blueprint KL16.1 comparison table A:19812 uses <=. No equivalence is silently assumed.
The current boundary volume predicate uses 10<distanceToBoundary; the KL16.1 Blueprint comparison uses distance>=10. Retain this buffer-convention comparison for the boundary adapter.
Shioya–Yamaguchi is the no-derivative route (KL92.1/Remark92.2), not a source for the derivative-controlled threshold contract.
Closed nonnegative components require the separate retained classification (Perelman lines1158–1181; KL printed2827). The finite-scale threshold does not absorb them.
